findings.reason: The standalone original tiles show only prose for the reachable cut in step 6.1. A two-region illustration materially clarifies the crucial orientation: no edges leave the reachable set, while exactly that set receives the +1 potential shift. It adds useful structure even though the proof is complete.
findings.action: Added a reachable-cut illustration and explanatory caption in the existing final Remarks section; the figure represents vertex sets rather than inventing particular graph edges.

correction: Added a TikZ picture of the no-path reachable cut T/R and its potential update, with the defining edge condition and four difference-update cases explained in adjacent prose.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Step 6.1 defines G on {1,...,r}, with edge k -> l iff some occurrence y has y_k-y_l=a_kl-1. The boxes represent T (reachable from t) and R (its complement), not individual vertices.
diagram_math_checks.check: The caption repeats that exact witness condition; no new concrete edge or witness is asserted.

diagram_math_checks.objects: The no-path branch assumes there is no directed path from t to r.
diagram_math_checks.check: The empty path puts t in T; absence of a t-to-r path puts r in R. If an edge left T for R, appending it to a path from t would put its target in T, contradiction. This justifies every membership and the no-edges T -> R label.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Integer potentials s and updated potentials hat s from step 6.1.
diagram_math_checks.check: hat s=s+1 on T and hat s=s on R, exactly as in step 6.1. Since a_kl=s_k-s_l, hat a_kl-a_kl is +1 on T x R, -1 on R x T and 0 within each part; since t is in T and r in R, hat a_tr=a_tr+1.
The existing proof, including its bound preservation argument, is byte-unchanged. The illustration is in Remarks and explicitly states that the rigorous proof remains independent.
